title: DC-area forecast: One or two strong storms into sunset; hot and mostly dry Sunday
subtitle: HAPPENING NOW: A few isolated to scattered strong storms remain possible through about 8 p.m. A couple of cells well west and southwest of DC are worth watching. Evening 80s dip to 70s for lows.
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: A few isolated to scattered strong storms remain possible through about 8 p.m. A couple of cells well west and southwest of DC, heading east toward Loudoun and Stafford counties, are worth watching. In those areas, make sure to take shelter should a severe thunderstorm warning be issued. Evening 80s dip to 70s for lows.

What's next? Hot but a little less humid Sunday with lower storm chances. Muggy and warm into the workweek. Partly to mostly sunny Sunday and Monday before higher showers and thunderstorm odds return Tuesday.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Any isolated to scattered storms try to end by about 8 p.m., then skies slowly clear. Muggy lows near 70 to mid-70s. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow (Sunday): Partly to mostly sunny skies and a bit less humid, but maybe not by much, with dew points still up in the 60s to near 70. Less moisture in the air may allow the air and ground to heat effectively, boosting highs near 90 to mid-90s. Most areas stay dry, though a pop-up afternoon shower or storm is possible, mainly south of DC. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow night: The heat simmers down a bit after sunset, but the humidity ticks upward. Overall it's warm and sticky with lows near 70 to mid-70s again. Mostly clear skies. Confidence: Medium-High

A look ahead

Highs climb into the low to mid-90s Monday and Tuesday. Heat indexes are once again near 100 both days, with sticky dew points still up near 70. Monday should be mostly sunny with an isolated late-day shower or storm possible. Partly sunny Tuesday with a chance of isolated to scattered showers or storms, mainly during the afternoon and evening hours. Confidence: Medium

A weak cold front currently looks to sink into the region Wednesday, bringing a chance for some rain in the morning and isolated afternoon storms. Highs aim for the mid-80s to around 90 under partly to mostly cloudy skies, and it's still fairly humid. Confidence: Medium

Temperatures are still warm Thursday and Friday with highs in the mid- to upper 80s. Humidity could come down (dew points falling to the mid- to upper 60s), if the front heads far enough south. We may still hang on to an isolated shower or storm chance. Confidence: Low-Medium

Today’s daily digit — 3/10: Feels-like temperatures reaching near 100, plus the chance for a few strong to severe afternoon storms, make today one to enjoy the A/C indoors. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

DC weather history for August 8

Extreme weather spans this date—from a record-shattering 1918 heat wave and a flooding 1942 deluge to oppressive, record heat again in 2007.
